article.title: The Hidden Cost of Subscription Convenience

paragraphs.en: Subscription services reduce friction. A small monthly payment can feel easier than a large one-time purchase, while automatic renewal makes it possible to keep using a service without repeated decisions. The same convenience can conceal waste. Customers may forget subscriptions they rarely use, and the cost of several modest payments can become substantial over a year. Good decisions require evaluating ongoing value, not merely whether the initial offer was attractive.
paragraphs.zh: 本段討論「The Hidden Cost of Subscription Convenience」的實務含義：先理解問題與決策背景。 重要的是將觀察到的現象與真正需要採取的行動分開，並留下可供驗證的依據。
paragraphs.ja: 「The Hidden Cost of Subscription Convenience」について、業務上の前提と意思決定を確認する。まず課題と背景を理解する。 観察事実と実際に取るべき行動を区別し、検証可能な根拠を残すことが重要である。

paragraphs.en: Consider the total cost across a full year, the frequency of actual use, and the effort required to cancel. A service that saves time every week may justify its price, while a rarely used service may not. It also helps to distinguish the cost already paid from the future cost you can still avoid. Past payments should not determine whether the next renewal is worthwhile.
